LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 13.3.1 WORD CLASSES: COMPOUND SENTENCES

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 13
Topic 13.3: Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Word Classes: Compound Sentences
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Word Classes: Compound Sentences, part of Strand 13 in Grade 8 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why do we join sentences? 2. How do we join sentences?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. read a text on the need for consumer protection and identify the compound sentences,

2. search online and offline for coordinating conjunctions to be used in constructing compound sentences, for example, but, or, and, so,

3. construct compound sentences on a variety of issues including consumer protection using different conjunctions,

4. join different independent clauses using a drag and drop application or a completion table, in groups,

5. display their sentences in class for peer review. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. read a text on the need for consumer protection and identify the compound sentences,
2. search online and offline for coordinating conjunctions to be used in constructing compound sentences, for example, but, or, and, so,
3. construct compound sentences on a variety of issues including consumer protection using different conjunctions,
4. join different independent clauses using a drag and drop application or a completion table, in groups,
5. display their sentences in class for peer review. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Word Classes: Compound Sentences together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication: It is enhanced as the learner communicates ideas clearly when using compound sentences.

• Digital literacy: It is fostered as the learner manipulates the drag and drop application.

Values:
Social justice: It is fostered as the learner provides support to peers through peer review.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Consumer protection: It is enhanced as the learner reads texts and constructs sentences on the theme.

• Effective communication: It is exhibited as the learner uses compound sentence to combine ideas.

Links to other Learning Areas:
The concept of constructing compound sentences is related to what learners learn in Kiswahili.
